_comment: Golden set for tuning retrieval against the RAW_DATA corpus (BNF 85, Oxford Handbook of Clinical Medicine, WHO EML). A chunk counts as a hit if it contains ALL terms in `expect_all` (when present) AND at least ONE term in `expect_any` (when present); matching is case-insensitive. Items without a `category` are the original easy baseline set.
_verification: Every item with "verified": false was written from general BNF knowledge and has NOT been checked against your corpus. For each one: (1) open the monograph named in `evidence`, (2) confirm the exact wording and number, (3) edit expect_all/expect_any to match how your chunker actually renders it (ranges use an en dash in the BNF; 'once daily' / '3 times a day' is BNF house style), (4) fill `answer_facts` from the page, (5) set verified to true. Do not trust a verified:false item as a benchmark.
_matching_notes: This file is ASCII-only on purpose (Windows cp1252 safe). Ranges are written with a hyphen; normalise en/em dashes and non-breaking spaces to plain '-' and ' ' in both chunk text and expected terms before matching, otherwise '5-10 mg' will miss '5–10 mg' in the BNF text. Short numeric terms like '2 g' also match '12 g'; prefer pairing them with a drug name in expect_all.
